items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I was talking about it last night with Anat, one of our tenor players.

ctx.x: Well that was something I was going to ask you about, especially being one of the things you do with IAJE. I attended the festival in January and it was breathtaking almost to see the amount of people and everybody there. But I wondered, is it translating down to that level of places to play and jam sessions and all that kind of thing?
It’s like it’s very bizarre but I can’t remember who I was speaking with, maybe somebody at IAJE but some other musicians, and they were saying the place of the jazz © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

artist is really going into academia now, and into the colleges. And you can tell by the way the students play. It’s so interesting that it’s — I won’t say cookie cutter — because all the kids, certain ones have different talents, but there’s so much information about how to learn. So much information and so little innovation, you know, in what the new artists, the young artists, are doing. It’s either duplicating styles or attitudes or whatever you call it, artists that came before them, or else it’s everybody…
